note: Reel 11: Dig Through India. Dig straight down from India and you come out in the Pacific, except a patch of desert outside Jaisalmer whose other side is Easter Island; then the dig, the heat, the 38-minute fall, and the root cause (only ~15% of land has land opposite). Original voice (Kokoro af_heart, speed 1.0). Numbers are written as spoken, so the display words match the voice's word tokens one to one. Indian names in phonemes: Jaisalmer /ʤˈIsᵊlmˌɛɹ/, Bengaluru /bˈɛŋɡəlˌuɹu/, Kolkata /kˈOlkətə/. Facts: docs/research.md.

lines.text: Dig straight down from India, and you'd think you'd hit America.
You won't. Delhi comes out in the Pacific. So do Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai and Kolkata.
lines.text_kokoro: You won't. Delhi comes out in the Pacific. So do Mumbai, [Bengaluru](/bˈɛŋɡəlˌuɹu/), Chennai and [Kolkata](/kˈOlkətə/).

lines.text: Almost all of India does. The big exception: a patch of desert outside Jaisalmer.
lines.text_kokoro: Almost all of India does. The big exception: a patch of desert outside [Jaisalmer](/ʤˈIsᵊlmˌɛɹ/).

lines.text: Its other side is Easter Island, and its giant stone heads.
Now dig. The deepest hole ever drilled is twelve kilometres. Barely a scratch.
lines.text_kokoro: Now dig. The deepest hole ever drilled is twelve kilometers. Barely a scratch.

lines.text: Below, it gets hotter, until the core: as hot as the surface of the Sun.
Now jump. You'd shoot through the centre faster than a satellite.
lines.text_kokoro: Now jump. You'd shoot through the center faster than a satellite.

lines.text: Thirty-eight minutes later, you'd pop out next to the stone heads.
The root cause of all those splashes? Only fifteen percent of land has land on its other side.
And with no air in the tunnel, you'd fall back. And forth. Forever.

ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet.
